terms.gloss: a conjugation: a class of verbs inflected alike; the inflection of a verb
evidence: Diom. p. 337 P.; Prisc. p. 836 P. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A term of the later grammarians (Comminianus in Charisius, Diomedes, Priscian) and of every Latin grammar since: verbum prīmae conjugātiōnis, a verb of the first conjugation (Traupman 227). In Cicero it is the kinship of words from one root (Top. 12, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: the conjugation of a verb; any inflection
evidence: Quint. 1.4.29: multa verba nōn tōtum dēclīnātiōnis ōrdinem ferunt
terms.comment: Varro’s and Quintilian’s word for the inflection of verbs as of nouns; Traupman calls it the more common term. To conjugate a verb is verbum dēclīnāre (Quint. 1.4.22; Traupman 227).

phrases.latin: quid? quod multa verba nōn tōtum dēclīnātiōnis ōrdinem ferunt? quaedam etiam mūtantur ut ferō in praeteritō
phrases.english: And what of the many verbs that do not have the whole series of the conjugation? Some even change, as ferō does in the perfect
Conjugate an active verb of the first conjugation.
What conjugation is it? — The fourth.
